findings.title: Missing await on reserve_stock in async reserve_fast
findings.explanation: reserve_fast is async but calls reserve_stock without await. The result is a coroutine object which is always truthy, so the 409 insufficient-stock branch never triggers and stock is never actually reserved. Also leaks unawaited coroutine.

evidence.why: async function calls reserve_stock without await, unlike reserve() above which uses await.

findings.title: Blocking requests.get in async handler without timeout
findings.explanation: async remote_stock uses blocking requests.get which blocks the event loop for all concurrent requests. No timeout means it can hang indefinitely, and no error handling for network failures.

evidence.why: Synchronous requests.get with no timeout inside async def blocks event loop.

findings.suggestion: Use httpx.AsyncClient with timeout, or make handler sync def with timeout and error handling.

findings.title: N+1 queries in order_details endpoint
findings.explanation: order_details fetches orders then queries items_for_order inside a for loop. Latency and DB load grow linearly with order count (N+1). Should batch fetch items for all order ids in one query.

evidence.why: Loop issues one db.items_for_order query per order.

findings.suggestion: Add bulk API like items_for_orders(conn, order_ids) and map results.

findings.title: Overlapping stock routes shadow each other
findings.explanation: /stock/{sku}/reserve-fast and /stock/remote/{sku} overlap: GET/POST to /stock/remote/reserve-fast matches both patterns with different bindings. First-registered route shadows the other, making behavior order-dependent and confusing.

evidence.why: Pattern /stock/remote/{sku} also matches same URL with sku=reserve-fast.
